message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after the lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts for repairs.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical).
• Must repair major defects within a reasonable time. | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or letter).
• If repairs are not made, you may withhold rent or seek a court order. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if needed. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month-to-month** tenants can terminate with **30 days’ notice**.
• Tenants can also terminate early if the landlord breaches the lease (e.g., fails to maintain habitability). | • Provide written notice (email or letter). | | **Entry by Landlord** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries; if you suspect unlawful entry, document it. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Privacy** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice or in a way that violates your privacy. | • Report any unlawful entry to local authorities or a housing attorney. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must keep common areas clean and safe. | • Report issues promptly; keep records. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but only if you follow proper procedures. | • Keep receipts and provide notice to the landlord. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the Texas eviction procedure (notice, filing, court order). | • Respond to notices; seek legal counsel if you believe the eviction is unlawful. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent control laws. | • Rent increases must be in accordance with the lease or local ordinances. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide utilities unless otherwise specified in the lease. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Subletting** | • Tenants may sublet only with landlord’s written consent, unless the lease allows it. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Insurance** | • Tenants are encouraged to carry renter’s insurance; landlords are not required to provide it. | • Consider renter’s insurance for personal property protection. | #### Practical Steps for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand all terms, including rent amount, due date, security deposit limits, and maintenance responsibilities. 2. **Keep Written Records** – Email or letter communications with the landlord, receipts for repairs, and a log of any issues. 3. **Know the Notice Periods** – For month-to-month leases, 30 days’ notice is standard; for fixed-term leases, check the lease end date. 4. **Report Problems Promptly** – Notify the landlord in writing and give them a reasonable time to fix the issue. 5. **Seek Legal Advice if Needed** – If you face eviction, discrimination, or other disputes, consult a Texas housing attorney or a local tenant advocacy group. #### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – The statutory law governing landlord-tenant relationships in Texas. - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – Handles discrimination complaints. - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** – Federal agency for housing rights. - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – Provide legal assistance and resources. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney in Texas.
